questions.question: What is a training and test split for?
options: To estimate performance on data the model has not seen
questions.explanation: Held out data is the only honest estimate of generalisation.

questions.question: What does overfitting look like?
options: High training error and high test error
Low training error and high test error
questions.explanation: An overfitted model memorises the training set and fails to generalise.

questions.question: Which metric is misleading on a heavily imbalanced dataset?
questions.explanation: Predicting the majority class always can give high accuracy while finding none of the minority cases.

questions.question: What does cross validation give you over a single split?
options: A more stable performance estimate across several folds
questions.explanation: K fold averages over multiple splits, reducing the variance of the estimate.

questions.question: What is the precision recall tradeoff?
options: Raising the decision threshold usually raises precision and lowers recall
Recall is precision on test data
questions.explanation: Tightening the threshold makes fewer, more confident positive predictions.

questions.question: What is data leakage?
options: Information from outside the training fold influencing the model, inflating scores
questions.explanation: Scaling before splitting, or using future information, leaks signal and produces unrealistic validation scores.

questions.question: Why does regularisation help generalisation?
options: It penalises large coefficients, constraining model complexity
questions.explanation: L1 and L2 penalties trade a little training fit for a simpler model that transfers better.

questions.question: What does the bias variance decomposition say about a very deep tree?
questions.explanation: An unpruned tree fits training data closely (low bias) but its predictions swing with the sample (high variance).

questions.question: Why should feature scaling be fitted on the training set only?
options: Fitting on all data leaks test set statistics into training
questions.explanation: The scaler is part of the model, so its parameters must come from training data alone.
